# Supermatter Structural Recovery
The Supermatter crystal continuously repairs structural damage over time.
Damage to the crystal creates unstable areas within its structure. These areas break down and release gaseous byproducts.
## Structural Recovery
After taking damage, the crystal gradually restores its structure.
The recovery process is always active and cannot be completely stopped. However, certain rare atmospheric compounds can influence the recovery rate.
Some gases can increase structural recovery, while others can reduce it. These effects modify the recovery speed but do not prevent regeneration entirely.
As long as structural recovery matches or exceeds incoming damage, the crystal remains stable.
If damage exceeds the recovery rate, stability will continue to decrease until a delamination event occurs.
## Gas Production
Damaged crystal material decomposes into Oxygen and Tritium.
These gases are released into the chamber while the crystal is under stress.
Atmospherics can collect and process these gases for station use.
Higher stress levels create larger amounts of damaged material, increasing gas production while also increasing strain on the crystal.
